v1_topic_builders_and_parser.detail: mqtt_topics_v1.hpp/.cpp: 7 DeviceId-keyed topic builders + 2 wildcard constants + parse_v1_device_id_from_topic(). Builders validate device_id_hex length only (callers are expected to already hold a trusted, pre-validated hex string, matching the DevicesApiDeviceSnapshot::device_id_hex precedent from HTTP v1); the parser does full validation (exact prefix/suffix, exactly 16 lowercase hex characters) for untrusted inbound topic text, directly reusing the same prefix+hex+suffix contract shape already proven out by web_ui::extract_uri_device_id_hex() in the HTTP v1 mutation-routes pass. Tested in test_mqtt_topics_v1.cpp: every builder's exact output string, both wildcard constants, undersized-buffer/null-arg rejection, and the parser's well-formed round-trip plus 6 distinct malformed-input rejection cases (wrong length short/long, uppercase, non-hex character, wrong prefix, wrong suffix).

v1_payload_serializers.detail: mqtt_serializer_v1.hpp/.cpp: state/availability/sensor(telemetry)/gateway-state serializers, each wrapping the schema_version/gateway_id/device_id/revision envelope. The sensor serializer reuses the legacy MqttSensorSnapshot struct verbatim rather than duplicating its field set, so it stays byte-for-byte consistent with what serialize_sensor_payload() already emits for the fields that carry over. The availability serializer is a deliberate format upgrade: the legacy availability payload is a bare retained string ("online"/"offline", not JSON at all), while v1 must be JSON to carry schema_version -- this is not a bug or oversight, it is required by plan #11's own schema_version requirement. Tested in test_mqtt_serializer_v1.cpp: every serializer's field content for both a full and an empty/default snapshot, and malformed-gateway_id/malformed-device_id/null-buffer rejection for all four.

deviations_from_literal_plan_text.deviation: Only plan items #10-#12 (topic root, DeviceId-keyed builders, versioned payload schema, topic parser) are implemented. Items #13-#15 (unsubscribe legacy command wildcards in production, publish retained tombstones for legacy topics, never recreate a legacy topic after cutover) are not implemented in this pass, and items #16-#19 (Home Assistant discovery migration, explicitly blocked on #10-#15 completing per item #19) are entirely unstarted.
deviations_from_literal_plan_text.why: Unlike the HTTP v1 mutation routes, MQTT has no plan-text exemption from production wiring in S4 (FD-19/#28-#29 name HTTP route registration and a management listener specifically). main/app_main.cpp already instantiates and unconditionally starts the live MqttBridge today (gated only by the mqtt_available capability), so implementing #13-#15 literally in this same pass would mean changing already-running production MQTT behavior -- unsubscribing real topics, publishing real retained tombstones to a real broker's retained-message state -- in the same change as designing the new schema. That is a materially different, higher-blast-radius risk category from building new, side-effect-free serialization/parsing code that nothing calls yet, and was judged to deserve its own dedicated, reviewable pass rather than being bundled in.
deviations_from_literal_plan_text.consequence: No regression: the live MQTT bridge's behavior (topics, payload shapes, retained state, HA discovery) is byte-for-byte unchanged by this pass, grep-verified. Every topic/payload primitive the cutover pass will need (builders, parser, serializers) already exists and is tested, so the cutover pass is a wiring change to mqtt_bridge.cpp/mqtt_device_sync.cpp rather than a new-contract-design problem.

deviations_from_literal_plan_text.deviation: No new architecture-gate rule (no INV-M0xx/INV-H0xx analogous to HTTP v1's INV-H010) proves that mqtt_bridge.cpp does not call the new v1 functions.
deviations_from_literal_plan_text.why: Unlike register_web_routes_v1() (a single named entry point that could be accidentally called from main/app_main.cpp), the v1 topic/serializer functions here are plain string-formatting/parsing utilities with 9+13 call sites across two files -- a grep-based check_absent rule naming every symbol would be brittle and would need updating on every future v1 helper added, for a foundation layer that currently has zero call sites anywhere. The actual risk this would guard against (someone wiring these into mqtt_bridge.cpp without doing the corresponding legacy-unsubscribe/tombstone work alongside it) is better caught by review at cutover time, when there is an actual behavior change to review.
deviations_from_literal_plan_text.consequence: Nothing currently prevents a future edit from calling these functions from mqtt_bridge.cpp without the full cutover being done. This is a judgment call, not an oversight, and is explicitly flagged for reconsideration once the cutover pass begins.
